title: Worker Threads vs Cluster vs Child

scenes.say: Ever wonder which Node.js concurrency model to use? Let's break down worker threads, clusters, and child processes so you can make the right call in interviews.

scenes.label: Workers
scenes.sub: Run JavaScript in multiple threads, sharing memory for heavy CPU tasks.
scenes.say: Worker threads let you run JavaScript in parallel threads. They're perfect for CPU-heavy tasks, and they can share memory between threads.

Clusters create multiple Node processes for load balancing, sharing the same server port. Child processes, on the other hand, run separate programs and are fully isolated—ideal for running scripts or shell commands.
Here's the cheat sheet: worker threads for CPU-bound JavaScript, clusters for scaling web servers, and child processes for running outside scripts.

scenes.question: Which model shares memory by default?
scenes.right: Only worker threads share memory by default. Clusters and child processes do not.
scenes.say: Quick check: which model shares memory by default? It's only worker threads. Clusters and child processes keep their memory separate.
